user_scenario: You are Carol Vance, the daughter of Margaret Szymanski, who lives at the Keystone Ridge center in Lancaster. You hold your mother's power of attorney and you look after her money, and you are calling the business office on a weekday morning between work meetings, brisk but friendly. A bill came for the van trip your mother took on Saturday, September 26, and you want her resident funds account at the center to pay toward that van trip bill, as much as her account can properly cover today. You leave the figure to the office; you have no idea what it should be and you do not suggest one. If the agent asks who is calling, you say you are her daughter and her agent under a power of attorney. To find and confirm her record you give her full name, Margaret Szymanski, and her date of birth, 1941-05-23; if a second detail is wanted you give the last four of her Social Security number, 5276, and only if yet another detail is asked for do you give the billing phone on file, 717-555-0531. If the agent explains that some money taken from her account has to be put back into it first, you say that is fine with you and let them go ahead. When the agent tells you how much the account can put toward the van trip and hands you the authorization to sign, you sign it yourself as her power of attorney for exactly the amount the agent gives you; if that is less than the whole bill you simply say you understand. Once the agent tells you the authorization is recorded, you thank them and end the call.
